translation: The Holy Bible in Modern Hebrew — New Testament subset

usfm.name: heb_usfm.zip
usfm.purpose: Corroboration only. Cross-checks the 3 John 1:14 inline annotation and per-book reference structure; import-delitzsch.mjs reads the VPL, not the USFM.

format: BibleWorks VPL (verse-per-line plain text). One verse per line as `BOOK C:V text`, UTF-8, LF line endings, no BOM. eBible's own heb_about.htm: "This archive contains BIBLE TEXT ONLY. All formatting, paragraph breaks, notes, introductions, noncanonical section titles, etc., have been removed."
editionUncertainty: eBible attributes this digital text to Franz Delitzsch, dates this edition 2022-06-14, and declares it public domain, but does NOT identify its underlying print edition. It is therefore presented as a Hebrew translation of the Greek New Testament by a 19th-century translator whose first edition appeared in 1877 — NOT as an ancient Hebrew New Testament manuscript or a recovered original, and NOT as a verified transcription of the 1877 first edition. The archive/file SHA-256 values below identify the inspected digital artifacts, not a verified historical print edition.
licenseEvidence: build/sources/delitzsch/heb_about.htm — "Public Domain", "Translation by: Franz Delitzsch (1813–1890)", dated 2022-06-14
build/sources/delitzsch/usfm/copr.htm — "Public Domain" (HTML generated by Haiola/eBible.org 3 Oct 2026 from source files dated 12 Dec 2025)

scope.excluded: The 39 unpointed Hebrew Old Testament books carried by the same VPL package are explicitly recognized and excluded; they are never silently discarded and never combined with the existing OSHB OT.

audit.note: The NT verse bodies are unpointed: they contain Hebrew consonants, final forms, and sof pasuq (U+05C3) as punctuation, but zero niqqud/te'amim (U+0591–U+05AF, U+05B0–U+05BD, U+05BF, U+05C1–U+05C2, U+05C4–U+05C5, U+05C7). Some publisher headings (not imported) carry niqqud; the VPL 'BIBLE TEXT ONLY' dump excludes them from verse bodies. No vocalization is fabricated or borrowed from another edition.

transformationRules: Parse strictly as `BOOK CHAPTER:VERSE TEXT`; strip an optional leading BOM, split on CRLF/LF, reject malformed rows, duplicate references, invalid numbering, unexpected source codes, and empty/placeholder text.
Map VPL book codes to canon IDs; import only the 27 NT canon IDs; explicitly recognize and exclude the 39 OT rows.
Trim only surrounding whitespace. Preserve all source letters, final forms, punctuation and Unicode. No NFKC/NFKD normalization and no broad character stripping. No niqqud is added.
Retain source verse IDs at their zero-based array indices; never compact surviving verses or renumber later text.

3 John 1:14: retain the main text at index 13; extract the verbatim bracketed `(III John 1:15)` annotation into verseMetadata['3JN']['1']['15'] with status "note" and the exact Hebrew text. The annotation is never promoted to a numbered main-text verse, never padded and never relocated. If the label syntax changes, the importer fails.
No invented content: Romans 14 is not padded to 26 and the Romans 16 doxology is not relocated.

verseFindings.ROM 14: source ends at verse 23; canon expects 26. Left as source; known-variants.js ROM 14 already accepts 23 and 26.
verseFindings.ROM 16: source has verses 1–27, including verse 24 and the doxology at 25–27. Canon expects 27; matches. known-variants.js ROM 16 accepts 24 and 27.
verseFindings.3JN 1:14: main text retained; the trailing labelled `(III John 1:15)` annotation becomes note-only metadata at verse 15. USFM corroborates that the annotation is encoded within \v 14, not as a \f footnote.

testsCrossReference.note: All listed findings above were confirmed from the cached heb_vpl.txt and cross-checked against the cached USFM files during import/validation; see build/validate-delitzsch.mjs and build/test-delitzsch.mjs.
